frontier.hypothesis: R2 closes when the tail base pseudo (p) loses its HARD conflict with hard reg $v0 and its $a0/$a1 preference set, at which point global.c's find_reg gives it $v0 and the scratch falls to $v1 -- the last nine instructions of the function.
frontier.mechanism: simulate.py --trace on the P4 body: a=78 pri=30000 calls=0 hard_conf=[2,29] prefs=[4,5] -> best=$a0. p is allocated FIRST (highest priority) and is barred from $v0 only by the hard conflict with reg 2; it then takes $a0 straight off its own preference list. Both are consequences of WHERE p's surviving live range sits and which hard-reg copies touch it -- neither is in inverse.py's atom space, which is why the depth-2 search returned FORECLOSED.
frontier.next_probe: On the P4 chassis run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80045878` and read the .greg/.flow dumps to find (a) exactly which insn range makes hard reg $v0 live simultaneously with p, and (b) which copy insn makes set_preference record $a0/$a1 for p -- do NOT guess either. Then move p's early mention to a block where $v0 is dead (candidates: inside the second `if (func_8004574C(s3) != 0) { func_800400F8(...); }` arm, or a store in the FIRST if's then arm) and re-run extract.py + simulate.py; success signature is a=78 with hard_conf lacking 2 and best=2.

frontier.hypothesis: R1' (idx 50) closes when reorg.c stops filling the `beq v1,v0` delay slot with `move a0,s3` copied from the branch target block -- target leaves a nop there.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c fills the branch delay slot from the successor block; ours can because `move a0,s3` at idx 53 is available and unconditionally safe. In target that fill did not happen, so at reorg time either the slot's candidate was not annullable/safe or the successor's first insn was not that copy.
frontier.next_probe: Read the .dbr/.sched2 dump on the P4 chassis for that branch (do not guess the pass). The likely C lever is changing what the third if's then arm leaves live -- e.g. whether `s3` is still the live call-argument pseudo at that point -- which the P4 then-arm change already perturbs; measure the P4 body with the then-arm early mention placed AFTER `s1[3] = 0` rather than before it, and with `p` typed/used so idx 53's copy is not the successor's first insn.

frontier.hypothesis: P4 is complete except for register assignment, so any remaining work must be graded on P4 (score 12, 108 insns), NOT on the score-10 candidate.c body (107 insns).
frontier.mechanism: The sandbox score is a weighted penalty; a body that is one instruction SHORT of target can score lower than a body with target's exact instruction stream and two register renames. Grading on the score-10 body is exactly what routed s3-s5 into the permuter dead end (s6 finding), and grading on the s6 chassis would now repeat the mistake one level up.
